p: בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ כְּתִיב: "וּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם הוֹצִיא לֶחֶם וָיָיִן",
— In this portion it is written: "And Malki-Tzedek king of Shalem brought out bread and wine,"
וְאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מג): "כָּל יַיִן שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה עוֹשֶׂה רוֹשֶׁם חוּץ מִזֶּה",
— and it is taught (in Bereishit Rabbah 43): "Every wine mentioned in the Torah leaves a negative mark except this one,"
וּפֵירֵשׁ הַמַּתְּנוֹת כְּהֻנָּה: שֶׁיָּצָא תַּקָּלָה, נֹחַ וּבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן וְכֵן כּוּלָּם.
— and the Matnot Kehunah explains: that a spiritual stumbling resulted, as with Noach and the sons of Aharon, and so all of them.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין, הָא נִמְצָא גַּם כֵּן בַּתּוֹרָה: "וַיִּשְׁתּוּ וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ",
— And one must understand, behold we also find in the Torah: "And they drank and became intoxicated with him," (Genesis 43:34),
שֶׁנֶּזְכַּר לֹא רַק שְׁתִיַּית יַיִן אֶלָּא שִׁכְרוּת!
— wherein there is mentioned not only the drinking of wine, but actual drunkenness!
גַּם בְּיִצְחָק כְּתִיב: "וַיָּבֵא לוֹ יַיִן וַיֵּשְׁתְּ";
— Furthermore, regarding Yitzchak it is written: "And he brought him wine, and he drank"; (Genesis 27:25);
וְכֵן בְּאַבְרָהָם כְּתִיב: "וַיַּעַשׂ אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל בְּיוֹם הִגָּמֵל אֶת יִצְחָק",
— and likewise concerning Avraham it is written: "And Avraham made a great feast on the day that Yitzchak was weaned," (Genesis 21:8),
וּסְתָם מִשְׁתֶּה הוּא יַיִן!
— and an unspecified feast (mishteh) centers upon wine!

h: In all sorrow there shall be profit

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן, דְּאִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת ל עַמּוּד ב):
— However, the inner matter is as taught (Berakhot 30b):
חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה קָא בָדַח טוּבָא,
— A sage saw his colleague rejoicing exceedingly,
אֲמַר לֵיהּ: "בְּכָל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר" כְּתִיב!
— he said to him: It is written, 'In all sorrow there shall be profit' (Proverbs 14:23)!
אֲמַר לֵיהּ: "אֲנָא תְּפִלִּין מַנַּחְנָא";
— He replied to him: 'I am wearing tefillin';
וְהַיְינוּ דִּתְפִלִּין מוֹרֶה שֶׁהוּא קָשׁוּר בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה,
— meaning that tefillin indicate that one is bound directly to the Primordial Thought,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "קֹדֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה' רֵאשִׁית תְּבוּאָתֹה וְגוֹמֵר",
— as it is stated: "Israel is holy unto Hashem, the firstfruit of His increase, etc.," (Jeremiah 2:3),
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב מִכֹּל וָכֹל,
— which occurs when one merits to align the heart completely and utterly,
וִישָׁרִים לְשִׂמְחָה, דִּכְתִיב: "לִישְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה".
— and the upright are destined for joy, as written: 'gladness is for the upright in heart' (Psalms 97:11).
וְכֵן בְּמִשְׁתֵּה אַבְרָהָם אִיתָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (שַׁבָּת קל עַמּוּד א) בְּשֵׁם פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
— And likewise regarding the feast of Avraham, it is brought in Tosafot (Shabbat 130a) in the name of Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer:
"בְּיוֹם הִגָּמֵל" – בְּיוֹם ה"ג מָל,
— on the day he was weaned—read: on the day that the 'Hei-Gimmel' (eight) was circumcised,
ח' דְּמִילָה,
— alluding to the eighth day of circumcision,
שֶׁיִּצְחָק הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה;
— for Yitzchak was the very first person circumcised on the eighth day;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהַתִּינוֹק נִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְנַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and since the infant is circumcised on the eighth day without conscious mind, becoming a Jew through this,
זֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
, — this demonstrates that he is bound at the root within the Primordial Thought.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 19:3: “Berakhot relates: He saw him rejoicing greatly and said, “It is written, ‘Rejoice with trembling.’” He answered, “I am wearing tefillin,” and so forth. What, seemingly, did he answer? It is forbidden to fill one’s mouth with laughter in this world, and it is written, “Then our mouth will be filled with laughter”—specifically then! But tefillin indicate that one is bound to the root of thought: “In the beginning”—for Israel, and so forth. Israel crowns the Holy One, blessed be He, with the splendor of tefillin, proclaiming “The Lord is one”; and the Holy One, blessed be He, praises Israel’s excellence, as stated there. This is “All the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you”—these are the tefillin of the head. Specifically “upon you”: the head tefillin are like a crown upon the head. The holy Zohar says that the word az, “then,” indicates when the light of Atika shines: the alef pierces the darkness, and so forth, and they reach the zayin—alef-zayin. This is “Then our mouth will be filled with laughter.” In the future the aspect called “He” will be revealed and shine; hence the expression “on that day,” when that aspect of “He,” indicating Atika, will shine like day. It is specifically “then” that our mouth will be filled with laughter. This is the answer “I am wearing tefillin”: when an Israelite puts on tefillin, a revelation of Atika’s light shines within him, because he is bound to the root. This too is “then,” as stated.”

h: The written and oral Torah and the Gemara’s teaching

p: וְכֵן כְּתִיב: "מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל",
— And likewise it is written: 'a great feast' (mishteh gadol),
וְאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה נג): "גְּדוֹל הָעוֹלָמִים הָיָה שָׁם";
— and it is taught (in Bereishit Rabbah 53): 'The Great One of the worlds was present there';
וְהוּא, דִּלְשׁוֹן "גָּדוֹל" בַּתּוֹרָה מוֹרֶה בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר,
— and that is because the term 'great' (gadol) in the Torah denotes that which is without measure,
דְּאִם לֹא כֵן לֹא נִקְרָא "גָּדוֹל", שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ הוּא קָטָן;
— for otherwise it cannot be termed truly great, since relative to that which is greater than it, it is small;
וּלְשׁוֹן "גְּדוֹל עוֹלָמִים" הַיְינוּ עַתִּיקָא.
— and the expression 'Great One of the worlds' refers to Atika Kadisha.
וְכֵן נִדְרָשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיט עַמּוּד ב) מִפָּסוּק זֶה
— And so it is expounded in the Gemara (Pesachim 119b) from this verse
עַל סְעוּדָה שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת לַצַּדִּיקִים וְכוּלֵי,
— concerning the banquet which the Holy One is destined to make for the righteous, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁסְּעוּדָה זוֹ הָיְתָה מֵעֵין סְעוּדַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא.
— meaning that this feast was an embodiment and foretaste of the banquet of the World to Come.
וּסְעוּדַת עוֹלָם הַבָּא הוּא כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר אֵין סוֹף, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא",
— And the banquet of the World to Come is when the Infinite Light (Ohr Ein Sof) will be unveiled, as is stated: 'In that day,'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה וְיָאִיר מִדַּת "הוּא" שֶׁהוּא הַנֶּעְלָם.
— which is when the attribute of 'He' (Hu)—the Supreme Concealed Realm—shall be revealed and illuminate.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ "מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל" שֶׁנִּרְמַז סְעוּדָה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
— And since 'a great feast' is expounded as hinting to the feast destined for the World to Come,
מִזֶּה מוּכָח שֶׁגַּם סְעוּדַת בְּרִית מִילָה הוּא מֵאוֹר עוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא "הוּא" שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אַחַר הַתִּיקּוּן;
— from this it is proven that the festive meal of a brit milah likewise derives from the light of the World to Come, designated 'Hu', which will manifest after universal rectification;
וְלָכֵן בִּסְעוּדַת בְּרִית מִילָה מוּתָּר הַיַּיִן הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ, וּלִישְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה,
— and therefore, at a brit milah celebration the gladdening wine is permitted, there being gladness for the upright in heart,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "זָכָה מְשַׂמְּחוֹ".
, — and as written: 'if he merits, it gladdens him.'

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 53:10: ““The child grew and was weaned. Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned” (Genesis 21:8). “The child grew and was weaned” – Rabbi Hoshaya the Great said: He was weaned from the evil inclination. The Rabbis say: He was weaned from his milk. “Abraham made a great feast” – Rabbi Yuda ben Rabbi Simon said: [This means that] the Great One of all worlds was present there. Rabbi Yudan bar Masparta said: “The king made a great feast” (Esther 2:18) – the great leaders of the world were there. That is what is written: “As the Lord will return to rejoice over you for good” (Deuteronomy 30:9) – in the days of Mordekhai and Esther, “as He rejoiced over your fathers” (Deuteronomy 30:9) – in the days of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Rabbi Yehuda ben Rabbi Simon said: “A great feast” – a feast of all the great people; Og and all the great men were there. They said to Og: ‘Did you not used to say: Abraham is like a barren mule and cannot beget a child?’ He said to them: ‘Now, what is his gift [Isaac], is it not puny? If I place my finger on him I could crush him.’ The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘Why are you disparaging his gift? By your life, you will [live to] see thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads emerging from his grandchildren, but that man [you, Og] will meet his end only by his hand,’ as it is stated: “The Lord said to Moses: Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand…” (Numbers 21:34). It is as Rabbi Levi said: A cradle was rocked first only in the house of Abraham our patriarch. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Menaḥama said: Those sixty-two kings that Joshua killed, all of them were at the feast of Abraham our patriarch. But were they not thirty-one? It is, rather, like what Rabbi Berekhya, Rabbi Ḥelbo, and Rabbi Parnakh said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: “The king of Jericho, one, [the king of Ai one, etc.]” (Joshua 12:9) — Why does the verse state: “One” [after each of the kings]? The explanation is that it refers to him and his viceroy.”

p: וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַיִּשְׁתּוּ וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ" הָיָה בִּסְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת,
— And likewise what is stated, 'and they drank and were intoxicated with him,' occurred at a Sabbath meal,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צב): "'וְהָכֵן' – וְאֵין 'הָכֵן' אֶלָּא שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי",
— as written (Bereishit Rabbah 92): 'and make ready (ve-hachen)'—'hachen' refers only to Shabbat, etc.,
וּבְשַׁבָּת מִתְגַּלֶּה הָרָצוֹן דְּעַתִּיקָא:
— and on Shabbat the supernal Will of Atika is unveiled:
בַּיּוֹם סְעוּדָתָא דְּעַתִּיקָא,
— by day is the meal of Atika Kadisha,
וּבִסְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא אָתְיָין לְסַעֲדָא בַּהֲדָהּ,
— and at the Friday night meal Atika Kadisha comes to dine with Her (the Shechinah),
וּמִתְגַּלֶּה הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא פְּנִימִיּוּת מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן,
— and Da'at, which is the inward essence of Keter Elyon, shines forth,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי מוּתָּר בּוֹ הַשְּׁתִיָּה.
— and for this reason drinking is permitted then.
וְזֶה הַטַּעַם שֶׁשָּׁתוּ אָז אֲחֵי יוֹסֵף,
— And this is the reason why the brothers of Yosef drank then,
אַף שֶׁלֹּא שָׁתוּ כָּל עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם שָׁנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה וּבַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קלט עַמּוּד א);
— even though they had abstained from drinking all twenty-two years of their separation, as noted in Bereishit Rabbah and the Gemara (Shabbat 139a);
אַךְ זֶה הוֹפִיעַ בָּהֶם יוֹסֵף קְדוּשַּׁת הַשַּׁבָּת,
— rather, Yosef radiated into them the holiness of Shabbat,
וְהִרְגִּישׁוּ קְדוּשַּׁת סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת וְשָׁתוּ.
— and they felt the supreme sanctity of the Sabbath meal and drank.
וְכַוָּנַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁהִשְׁקָה אוֹתָם,
— And Yosef's intention in plying them with drink
שֶׁרָצָה לֵידַע מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם אִם קְשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
— was that he wished to test the inner depths of their hearts to verify if they were bound to the Root,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין: "אַגְבָּרוּ חַמְרָא וְכוּלֵי, נִכְנַס יַיִן יָצָא סוֹד".
, — akin to what they said in Sanhedrin: 'Give wine... wine enters, the secret comes out.'

Through his displacement the inwardness of his heart will become known, and the good depths of his heart will come into action. He is to conceal the deficiency at the root, so that it does not spread outward and will consequently perish. A person reaches this through his service of the blessed God by entering the actions and affairs of this world; through this, what a person is becomes recognizable. Thus the Talmud says: “A person is recognized in three things: his cup, his purse, and his anger.” It does not give as a sign for recognizing someone the time when he stands in the synagogue wrapped in a mitzvah tallit and crowned with tefillin, implying that this provides no proof. The principal recognition comes when he enters the concealments of worldly affairs, dealing with people in the markets and streets. Then one can recognize a person’s preciousness: what lies in the depths of his heart.”

h: Intoxication and the Holiness of Purim

p: וְעִנְיַן הַשִּׁכְרוּת הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (מְגִילָּה ז עַמּוּד ב): "מִיחַיַּיב אִינִישׁ לִבְסוֹמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא וְכוּלֵי",
— And the concept of spiritual intoxication is like that which we find (Megillah 7b): "A person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim, etc.,"
אַף שֶׁלֹּא מָצִינוּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה רַק לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן,
— even though elsewhere in holy service we find only drinking wine,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מָצִינוּ בְּרַב נַחְמָן שֶׁאָמַר: "כָּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא שָׁתֵינָא רְבִיעֲתָא דְּחַמְרָא לָא צִילָאי דַּעְתַּאי",
— wherein we find that Rav Nachman said: 'As long as I have not drunk a revi'it of wine my mind is not clear,'
אֲבָל לֹא "לִבְסוֹמֵי" שֶׁמְּבַלְבֵּל הַדַּעַת!
— but never intoxication that confounds conscious intellect!
אַךְ בִּמְחִיַּת עֲמָלֵק שֶׁהוּא רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה,
— However, at the obliteration of Amalek, who represents the first and head of the impure shells,
וְאָז מִתְבָּרְרִין יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁקְּשׁוּרִים בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה;
— then Israel are demonstrated to be bound directly in the Primordial Thought;
וְכֵן נִדְרָשׁ: "'לַיְּהוּדִים הָיְתָה אוֹרָה וְשִׂמְחָה וְשָׂשׂוֹן וִיקָר' – 'וִיקָר', אֵלּוּ תְּפִלִּין וְכוּלֵי",
— and so it is expounded: 'To the Jews there was light and gladness and joy and honor'—'honor' refers to tefillin, etc.,
וּתְפִלִּין שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ מוֹרֶה שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְשׁוּרִים בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה.
— and the tefillin on the head demonstrates that Israel are bound within the Primordial Thought.
וּכְשֶׁמִּתְבָּרֵר זֶה, אָז יֵשׁ גַּם שִׁכְרוּת בִּקְדוּשָׁה;
— And when this is revealed, then even drunkenness exists in holiness;
וְכֵן הִרְגִּישׁוּ אָז הַשְּׁבָטִים הַקְּדוּשָׁה בִּסְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת שֶׁעָשָׂה יוֹסֵף לָהֶם.
, — and thus did the Tribes then sense that transcendent sanctity at the Sabbath meal that Yosef prepared for them.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Yisrael Kedoshim 7:36: ““Esther—the end of all the miracles” is the culmination of the holiness of the appointed times, reaching the holiness of a day without cessation from labor. They did not accept it as a festival [prohibiting labor], but only as “feasting and joy.” Its end is bound to the beginning of the holiness of the appointed times: the holiness of Shabbat, the beginning of all miracles in the creation of the entire world from nothing. All this was for Israel, although it did not arise through their awakening or their sanctification, since they were not yet in the world. At the end, the days of Purim, it was revealed that even all the holiness of “Israel sanctifies the appointed times” does not come from themselves and their effort, but entirely from the holiness fixed and enduring within them. This is clarified at the time of intoxication “until he does not know,” as explained above: their very essence is revealed as entirely holy to the Lord.”

h: The forefathers and wine and spiritual joy

p: וְכֵן מַה דִּכְתִיב בְּיִצְחָק: "וַיָּבֵא לוֹ יַיִן וַיֵּשְׁתְּ",
— And likewise that which is written of Yitzchak, "and he brought him wine and he drank," (Genesis 27:25),
שָׁם כְּתִיב: "וָאֹכַל מִכֹּל",
— there it is written: "and I ate of all," (Genesis 27:33),
וְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יז עַמּוּד א):
— and it is taught in the Gemara (Bava Batra 17a):
"שְׁלֹשָׁה הִטְעִימָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכוּלֵי, יִצְחָק דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ 'מִכֹּל'",
— "Three individuals the Holy One gave a foretaste of the World to Come in this world, etc., Yitzchak, concerning whom it is written 'of all',"
וְאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סז): "'וָאֹכַל מִכֹּל' – מִכָּל טוֹב שֶׁהוּא מְתוּקָּן לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא";
— and it is taught (in Bereishit Rabbah 67): 'and I ate of all'—of all goodness prepared for the World to Come';
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁזָּכָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע – הוּתַּר לוֹ הַיַּיִן.
— and since he merited a foretaste of the World to Come in this world, free from the evil inclination, wine was permitted unto him.

h: Avraham’s Growth and the Wine of a Mitzvah

p: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאַבְרָהָם, שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה לְמִדַּת "בַּכֹּל" רַק אַחַר דִּכְתִיב: "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים",
— In contrast to Avraham, who did not attain the attribute of 'bakol' (in all) until after it is written: 'And Avraham was old, advanced in days,' (Genesis 24:1),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קכט עַמּוּד ב): "אַבְרָהָם לָא עָאל בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין עַד דַּהֲוָה סִיב וְכוּלֵי",
— and as written (Zohar I 129b): 'Avraham did not enter into those supernal days until he was old, etc.,'
"יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין" הַיְינוּ ג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
— supernal days referring to the three higher sefirot,
וְזֶה זָכָה רַק אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן עֲשִׂירִי;
— and this he achieved only after the tenth trial (the Akeidah);
וְכָאן דְּהָיָה עוֹד קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּימּוֹל וְלֹא זָכָה לְמִדַּת "בַּכֹּל" – לֹא הוּתַּר לוֹ הַיַּיִן.
— whereas here, where it was still before he circumcised himself and had not yet merited the attribute of 'bakol,' wine was not permitted unto him.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "כָּל יַיִן שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה עוֹשֶׂה רוֹשֶׁם חוּץ מִזֶּה",
— And this is why they stated: 'Every wine written in the Torah leaves a mark except this one,'
שֶׁמִּכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא יָצָא תַּקָּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ.
— for nonetheless no spiritual stumbling emerged from it.
וְהַטַּעַם, שֶׁאַף יַיִן זֶה הָיָה יַיִן דְּמִצְוָה,
— And the reason is that even this wine was a wine of mitzvah,
דְּאִיתָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י בְּשֵׁם מִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: שֶׁרָמַז לוֹ עַל הַמְּנָחוֹת וְעַל הַנְּסָכִים וְכוּלֵי,
— for it is cited in Rashi's commentary in the name of the Midrash: that he hinted to him concerning the meal-offerings and libations, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא עא עַמּוּד א): "הָרוֹצֶה לְנַסֵּךְ יַיִן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ – יְמַלֵּא גְּרוֹנָם שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַיִן",
— and this is based upon what is written (Yoma 71a): 'He who desires to pour wine upon the Altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine,'
וְאִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת י עַמּוּד ב): "כָּל הַמְאָרֵחַ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְכוּלֵי מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ מַקְרִיב תְּמִידִין";
— and it is taught (Berakhot 10b): 'Whoever hosts a Torah scholar, Scripture accounts it unto him as if he offered the daily continuous sacrifices';
וְהוּא, כְּשֶׁמַּאֲכִיל לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם בָּשָׂר הוּא כְּמַקְרִיב תְּמִידִין,
— and this means, when he feeds a Torah scholar meat it is as offering daily animal sacrifices,
וּכְשֶׁמַּאֲכִילוֹ לֶחֶם הוּא כְּמַקְרִיב מְנָחוֹת;
— and when he feeds him bread it is like offering meal-offerings;
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רִאשׁוֹן,
— and Avraham our Father was the very first Torah scholar,
שֶׁקִּיֵּים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּתְּנָה,
— who observed the entire Torah before it was formally given,
וּמֵהֵיכָן לָמַד הַתּוֹרָה?
— and from where did he learn the Torah?
אֶלָּא נַעֲשׂוּ שְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו כְּמִין שְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וְהָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה,
— rather his two kidneys became like two rabbis, welling forth and teaching him Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא),
— as written (in Bereishit Rabbah 61),
וְהָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רִאשׁוֹן;
— and he was the premier Torah scholar;
וּכְשֶׁהֶאֱכִילוֹ שָׁם רָמַז לוֹ עַל הַמְּנָחוֹת וְהַנְּסָכִים.
— and when Shem fed him there, he hinted to him concerning the meal-offerings and libations.

h: Malki-Tzedek’s Bread and Wine as Priestly Service

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "וּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק וְגוֹמֵר הוֹצִיא לֶחֶם וָיָיִן, וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן",
— And this is what Scripture states: "And Malki-Tzedek, etc., brought out bread and wine, and he was a priest to the Most High God,"
וְלִכְאוֹרָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר: "וּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן הוֹצִיא וְגוֹמֵר"!
— and seemingly it should have said: 'And Malki-Tzedek king of Shalem, and he was a priest to the Most High God, brought out, etc.'!
אַךְ פֵּירוּשׁ הַכָּתוּב "וְהוּא כֹהֵן וְגוֹמֵר",
— Rather, the meaning of 'and he was a priest, etc.' is
שֶׁבִּשְׁעָתָהּ שֶׁהוֹצִיא לֶחֶם וָיַיִן הָיָה שָׁם כֹּהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן,
— that at the precise time that he brought out bread and wine, he acted as a priest to the Most High God,
שֶׁהָיָה הַמְּכֻוָּון שֶׁלּוֹ לְהַקְרִיב לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם לֶחֶם וָיַיִן שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב כִּמְנָחוֹת וּנְסָכִים,
— his holy intent being to present to a Torah scholar bread and wine which are reckoned like meal-offerings and libations,
וְהוּא בִּבְחִינַת כֹּהֵן הַמַּקְרִיב.
— he himself functioning in the capacity of the officiating priest.

h: Avraham’s Sorrow and the Purpose of Egyptian Exile

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ:
— And afterward it is brought in the Midrash:
אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: "אַף זֶה לֹא יָצָאנוּ מִיָּדוֹ, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם קָרָא עָלָיו 'וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם'",
— Rabbi Levi said: 'Even from this we did not emerge unscathed from his hand, for from there He decreed upon him: "and they shall serve them, and they shall afflict them"';
וּבְוַדַּאי שֶׁאֵין הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהַיַּיִן גָּרַם גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם לְעוֹנֶשׁ,
— and certainly the meaning is not that the wine caused the Egyptian exile as a punitive retribution;
רַק הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים לב עַמּוּד א):
— rather it is akin to what they expounded (Nedarim 32a):
מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶעֱנַשׁ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ וְנִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ בָּנָיו לְמִצְרַיִם מָאתַיִם וָעֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים?
— Why was Avraham our Father punished that his descendants were enslaved to Egypt for two hundred and ten years?
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעָשָׂה אַנְגַּרְיָא בְּתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְכוּלֵי,
— Because he drafted Torah scholars into forced military service, etc.,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִפְרִיז עַל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי,
— because he questioned the divine attributes of the Holy One, etc.,
שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ בְּנֵי אָדָם מִלְּהִכָּנֵס תַּחַת כַּנְפֵי הַשְּׁכִינָה וְכוּלֵי;
— or because he prevented the captives of Sodom from entering beneath the wings of the Shechinah, etc.;
וְלִכְאוֹרָה יֵשׁ לְהָבִין, מַה חָטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה?
— and seemingly one must understand: what was the sin of Israel that they should be subjugated for this?
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת, גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה לְטוֹבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— However in truth, the Egyptian exile was for the ultimate good of Israel,
שֶׁהָיָה הֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
— serving as the spiritual crucible preparing them for the Giving of the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ה עַמּוּד א): "שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת נָתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכוּלָּן לֹא נְתָנָן אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי",
— as written (Berakhot 5a): 'Three precious gifts did the Holy One give to Israel, and none was given except through suffering, and these are: Torah, etc.,'
וְעַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין שֶׁבְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם זָכוּ לַתּוֹרָה.
— and through the afflictions in the Egyptian exile they merited the Torah.
אַךְ הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁנֶּעֱנַשׁ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם – שֶׁהוֹדִיעוּהוּ גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, וְעַבְדוּת "וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם",
— Rather, the explanation is that Avraham was punished by being informed of the Egyptian exile and the bitter servitude 'and they shall serve them and afflict them,'
וְעַל זֶה הָעוֹנֶשׁ נֶחְלְקוּ בַּגְּמָרָא בְּטַעֲמוֹ.
, — and regarding the rationale for this sorrowful disclosure the sages in the Gemara differed.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 27:4: ““This bitter herb that we eat,” and so forth, “because the Egyptians embittered our ancestors’ lives.” The matter of bitter herbs is like what we find in the holy Zohar: had Israel not descended to Egypt and been refined there, they would not have been His unique people. It is written, “When the Most High allotted nations,” and “For the Lord’s portion is His people”; Israel was already the Lord’s portion from the generation of the Dispersion. This is “Had they not descended to Egypt”: they were there under intense concealment, as it is written, “You know how we lived in the land of Egypt,” and “You saw their abominations and their idols.” Nevertheless, they had the power to restrain themselves. h: Avraham’s devotion and the holiness of Israel

p: וְהִנֵּה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ בֶּאֱמֶת נִכְלַל בּוֹ אֻמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
— And behold Avraham our Father genuinely encompassed within himself the entire nation of Israel,
וְגַם נַעֲשָׂה אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנִּקְרָא "אֵיתָן הָאֶזְרָחִי" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא טו עַמּוּד א),
— and was also established as a native citizen of Israel, called 'Eitan HaEzrachi' (Bava Batra 15a),
וְנִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן "יִשְׂרָאֵל" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה;
— and was likewise designated 'Yisrael' as brought in Bereishit Rabbah;
אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא "תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים" (חֲגִיגָה ג עַמּוּד א);
— yet nonetheless he is titled 'the first of the converts' (Chagigah 3a);
וְזֶה שֶׁהוֹדִיעוּהוּ בְּכָאן גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם,
— and this is why He announced to him here the Egyptian exile,
וּבַסּוֹף: "וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל",
— and at the culmination: 'and afterward they shall go out with great wealth' (Genesis 15:14),
וְ"גָדוֹל" מוֹרֶה עַל מִדּוֹת עַתִּיקָא,
— and 'great' denotes the attributes of Atika Kadisha,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמְּקֻשָּׁרִין בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
— meaning that they are bonded directly at the Root;
וְזֶה הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם,
— and this was the transcendent 'great wealth' that they brought forth out of Egypt,
שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ שָׁם עַל יְדֵי הָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת,
— in that they were refined there through the Ten Plagues across all ten sefirotic attributes,
שֶׁבְּכָל מַכָּה יָצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּדָּה אַחַת בַּקְּלִיפָּה,
— such that with each plague Israel were extracted from one impure attribute of the klipah,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ גַּם כֵּן עֶשֶׂר זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה,
— as there exist ten opposing forces mirroring the holy,
וְנִכְנְסוּ בִּקְדוּשָׁה בְּמִדָּה אַחַת,
— and entered within holiness into that corresponding attribute,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, לו עַמּוּד א): "נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל".
— reflecting that which is written in the holy Zohar (II 36a): 'a smiting unto Egypt and a healing unto Israel.'

h: Wine and spiritual joy and the exile and redemption

p: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה אַרְבַּע כּוֹסוֹת בְּפֶסַח,
— And so we find that our Sages of blessed memory instituted four cups of wine on Passover,
אַף שֶׁהוּא שִׁיעוּר שִׁכְרוּת,
— even though this constitutes an intoxicating quantity,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת סה עַמּוּד א): "אַרְבַּע – אֲפִילּוּ חֲמוֹר תּוֹבַעַת וְכוּלֵי",
— as we find (Ketubot 65a): 'Four cups—she may even demand a donkey, etc.,'
וְלָמָּה תִּקְּנוּ שִׁיעוּר שִׁכְרוּת?
— and why would the Sages establish a measure of intoxication?
אַךְ בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַכָּה עֲשִׂירִית שֶׁהֵם "בְּנִי בְכֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
— Rather, at the Exodus from Egypt when Israel were refined at the tenth plague as 'My son, My firstborn, Israel' (Exodus 4:22),
וּ"בְנִי" הַיְינוּ שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
— and 'My son' signifies being bound at the essential Root,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת לְהָרַמַּ"ע: "נֶפֶשׁ הָאָב מַזָּל לַבֵּן",
— as written in Asarah Maamarot by the Rama MiFano: 'the soul of the father is the mazal (supernal source) of the son,'
וּמַזָּלָא הַיְינוּ עַתִּיקָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, עט עַמּוּד ב),
— and Mazal corresponds to Atika Kadisha (Zohar III 79b),
וְלָכֵן בָּאָה הַמִּצְוָה בְּיַיִן בְּשִׁיעוּר שִׁכְרוּת, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָׁה.
, — and therefore the mitzvah was formulated with wine to the point of drunkenness, which is likewise in holiness.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Achrei Mot 74:408-410 (III 79b): “Rabbi Shimon said: It is written, “From new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath.” Why is one equated with the other? Because all ascend to one level; one unites with the other. Their mutual joy is found only when the Holy Ancient One is revealed, and then there is joy for all. We learned: It is written, “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day”—for the Sabbath day itself, praise with which the Holy One, blessed be He, is praised. Then joy is found and an additional soul is given, for the Ancient One is revealed and union is made ready. So, too, at the renewal of the moon, for the sun shines upon her with the joy of the Ancient One’s radiance above. Therefore this offering is above, so that everything may be sweetened and joy found in the world. Thus, “Bring an atonement for Me”—the wording is precise. It was taught: It is written, “The Sabbath burnt offering on its Sabbath, above the daily burnt offering,” for one must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Thus “above the daily burnt offering” is precise. It was taught: Concerning Hannah it is written, “She prayed above the Lord”—“above” specifically, because children depend upon the holy mazal, as we have explained. There is no word in the Torah, nor even a small letter in the Torah, that does not allude to supernal wisdom and from which heaps upon heaps of the mysteries of supernal wisdom do not depend, as it is written: “His locks are curling heaps,” as has been stated.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Peri Tzadik, Pesach 15:3: “Through Shabbat one repairs the past. “It gladdens” means “Joy for the upright of heart”: one merits straightness of heart, so that both hearts are only good, emptying the evil from the fool’s heart until everything is very good. Therefore, in the passage of the omer, which comes from barley to clarify that even one whose actions resemble an animal’s is nevertheless intended to become “very good”—light emerging from darkness—this festival is specifically called simply “Shabbat.” Wine in an amount that produces intoxication also occurs in it, to clarify Israel, who is recognized through his cup: in Israel [wine] is “If he merits, it gladdens him,” as stated in Yoma, for he merits straightness of heart. As we have said, eating on this festival comes in holiness, with the blessing “Who sanctified us through His commandments.” It repairs the root of the damage that occurred through eating, when the curse was “You shall eat the plants of the field.” The changed practice of dipping vegetables addresses this, which was a cause of “They embittered their lives with hard labor.” Afterward comes the commandment of eating matzah, nullifying the leaven in the dough. We recite “Who sanctified us through His commandments” over these acts of eating; this itself brings holiness to Israel, and through it all the eating of the entire year is repaired to be in holiness.”

Just as the blessed God acts at that time to illuminate salvation for Israel in stages—as in “Then He saw it, recounted it, prepared it, and also examined it,” four stages—so the person is obliged to prepare himself in correspondence with that divine will, to become a vessel for receiving salvation from the blessed God. The principal preparation of the vessel is to illuminate eyes within the kingdom of Heaven, for the kingdom of Heaven has no eyes, and the person must introduce eyes into it. As our Sages said concerning the cup of Kiddush over wine: a person must direct his eyes toward it. That is, he should see within every concealment the truth that the blessed God alone governs there too. Therefore they said: “Wine—some drink it and it is bad for them ... for a Torah scholar it is always good.” Since the Torah scholar can show God’s governance within every forgetting and concealment, he has a vessel for receiving wine, and drinks it to his good.”

h: I will make you a great nation

p: וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה כָּלוּל בּוֹ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל",
— And Avraham our Father, who encompassed the Congregation of Israel, concerning which it was said 'and I will make you a great nation,'
זָכָה גַּם כֵּן לְמִדַּת גְּדוּלָּה, וּמִלַּת "גָּדוֹל" מוֹרָה עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ;
— merited likewise the attribute of Gedulah, and the word 'great' extends up to the Root;
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁזֶּה זָכָה רַק אַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁבָּא בַּיָּמִים וְנִקְרָא "אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל",
— yet since he attained this only later when advanced in days and confirmed as a native in Israel,
וְכָאן קוֹדֶם הַמִּילָה לֹא זָכָה עֲדַיִן לָזֶה וְלֹא זָכָה לְמִדַּת "בַּכֹּל",
— whereas here, prior to circumcision, he had not yet attained this and had not merited the trait of 'bakol,'
הוֹדִיעוּהוּ שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ בָּנָיו בְּמִצְרַיִם קוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל.
— He informed him that his descendants would be enslaved in Egypt before meriting that great wealth.
וְזֶה כַּוָּנַת רַבִּי לֵוִי: "שֶׁלֹּא יָצָאנוּ רֵיק מִזֶּה",
— And this is the meaning of Rabbi Levi: 'we did not emerge empty from this,'
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ "וַעֲבָדוּם וְגוֹמֵר",
— as it was told to him 'and they shall serve them, etc.,'
וַעֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לַיַּיִן.
— for as yet he was not spiritually fit for that level of wine.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 9:1: “The blessed God fixed the service Abraham our father performed each day. On the following day, the previous day’s service became concealed from him because it had been fixed completely within his heart and had become like a garment for him. Thus all Abraham’s acts of service, each in its day, became garments; afterward, on the following day, a new order of service began for him. From that concealment, in which yesterday’s service became hidden and became “supernal days, days known through the mystery of faith,” the principal building of the world was formed. The world is called olam from he’elem, concealment, as it is written, “He also placed the olam in their hearts.” Of this it is written: “I remember for you the kindness of your youth, the love of your bridal days, your following after Me.” As a person’s acts of service become concealed and fixed within the garments of this world, the person is afterward drawn, with all his garments, after God’s will even without his conscious knowledge. This is called “your following after Me.””

h: The written and oral Torah and wine and spiritual joy

p: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּתִיב בַּתּוֹרָה: "הוֹצִיא לֶחֶם וָיָיִן, וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן",
— And nevertheless it is written in the Torah: "He brought out bread and wine, and he was a priest to the Most High God,"
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ: "הִלְכוֹת כְּהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה גִּלָּה לוֹ:
— and upon this they expounded in the Midrash: 'The laws of the High Priesthood he revealed to him:
לֶחֶם – זֶה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים, וְיַיִן – אֵלּוּ הַנְּסָכִים";
— 'bread' refers to the Showbread, and 'wine' refers to libations';
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הַמְּכֻוָּון שֶׁל שֵׁם הָיָה לְהַקְרִיב כְּמוֹ כֹּהֵן,
— meaning that in truth the intention of Shem was to offer like a priest,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת נִכְלַל בּוֹ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— since Avraham genuinely embodied the sanctity of Israel,
וְהוּא הָיָה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רִאשׁוֹן וְכָאָמוּר, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת.
— and he was the premier Torah scholar as stated, both facets being true.
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר מַה שֶּׁהִזְכִּיר הִלְכוֹת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
— And one must clarify why the Midrash specifically mentions the laws of the High Priest,
אַף דְּלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים וּנְסָכִים שָׁוִין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט;
— since the Showbread and libations are performed equally by an ordinary priest and a High Priest;
אַךְ נֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּשֵׁם: "וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן",
— rather, it corresponds to what is written of Shem: 'and he was a priest to the Most High God,'
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל עַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת "עֶלְיוֹן" עַל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— which points to Atika Kadisha, which is the transcendent attribute 'Elyon' above Havayah, as written in the Zohar,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ גַּם בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִמִּדָּתוֹ שֶׁהוּא כֹּהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן,
— meaning that he radiated into Avraham from his attribute of being a priest to El Elyon,
וְזֶה מוֹרֶה מַדְרֵגַת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל;
— and this characterizes the spiritual tier of the High Priest;
וְזֶה הוֹפִיעַ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
— and this shone within Avraham our Father,
וְלָכֵן אָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ גַּם כֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ: "הֲרִימֹתִי יָדִי אֶל ה' אֵל עֶלְיוֹן".
— and therefore Avraham likewise said afterward: "I have lifted my hand unto Hashem, God Most High" (Genesis 14:22).
